svg.title: Why the HTML looks empty: static source versus the JavaScript-rendered DOM
svg.desc: Fetching a modern page two ways. With requests or urllib you get the initial HTML, which is often just a shell: an empty app div plus a script tag, so the product data is not there yet and BeautifulSoup finds nothing. With a real headless browser such as Selenium, the page's JavaScript runs, fetches data by an XHR call to an API like /api/products, and builds the full DOM, so after an explicit wait the data is present and you can scrape it. The shortcut: that XHR usually returns clean JSON, so you can open DevTools Network, find the /api/products request, and call it directly with requests, skipping the browser entirely for a much faster scrape. Render only when you can't find the underlying API.
svg.text: “The HTML is empty” — you're seeing the page before its JavaScript runs
GET shop.com/products
requests.get(url) — static source
<script src="bundle.js"></script>
← no product data in the markup
BeautifulSoup parses this and finds nothing —
the data hasn't been rendered yet.
Headless browser — renders it
1. loads page → runs the JavaScript
2. JS fetches XHR /api/products
3. builds the full DOM — data now present
Explicit-wait for the element, then scrape
(a real browser is heavy — use only when needed)
The fast path: skip the browser, call the API the page already calls
That XHR almost always returns clean JSON. Open DevTools → Network, find the /api/products request, and
requests.get() that endpoint directly — no rendering, structured data, often 10× faster and far more stable.
Advanced scraping starts with one question: is this content in the HTML, or built by JavaScript? If it's static, plain
HTTP + a parser is fastest. If it's dynamic, prefer the hidden JSON API when you can find it, and fall back to driving
a headless browser only when the data truly exists only after rendering (heavy JS apps, canvas, anti-scrape shells).
